question.problem:
Given that 
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}4xy-3{y}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}4xy-3{y}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=4xy-3{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2{x}^{2}-6xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy-3{y}^{2})=4y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}-6xy)=4x-6y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4xy-3{y}^{2})=4x-6y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}-6xy)=-6x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4y & 4x-6y \\ 4x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,1)=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,1)=4\cdot (-6)-(-2)\cdot (-2)=-28.
$$
